title: Two Bookings That Never Clash
statement:
A venue gets booking offers offers[i] = [start, end, pay]. An offer occupies every day from start to end, both included, and earns pay.

You may accept at most two offers, and two accepted offers must not share a day. So if one ends on day d, the other can start on day d + 1 at the earliest. Return the largest total pay you can earn.

examples.why: The first two share day 3. Taking [3, 5] and [6, 8] earns 6 + 3.
The best pair only earns 2 + 3 = 5. One long booking alone pays more.
Two short bookings on days 2 and 3 beat the single best offer of 9.

hints: Fix the earlier of the two bookings. What do you want from the later one?
For a booking ending on day e, you want the best pay among offers starting on day e + 1 or later. If offers are sorted by start, those form a suffix.
Sort by start and build a suffix maximum of pay. For each offer, binary search for the first start > its end and add the suffix maximum there. Also consider each offer alone.

explain.intuition:
In any valid pair, one booking finishes before the other starts. Fix that earlier booking with end day e. The partner can be any offer starting after e, and you simply want the best-paying one among them.

Sort the offers by start day. "Starts after e" is then a suffix of the sorted list, found with one binary search, and a precomputed suffix maximum gives the best pay in that suffix in O(1). Try every offer as the earlier booking, add its partner's best pay (or nothing), and keep the maximum. Taking a single offer is covered by adding 0 when no partner exists.
steps: Build best[i] = the largest pay among sorted offers i..n−1, with best[n] = 0.
For each offer [s, e, p], binary search the first index j whose start is greater than e.
pitfalls: Treating touching offers as compatible. Ends are inclusive, so [1, 5] and [5, 9] clash.
Forcing exactly two offers. One big booking can beat every pair.
Searching for start ≥ end instead of start > end. That is the same off-by-one as above.

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: Try each offer alone and each compatible pair.

solutions.title: Sort by start, suffix maximum, binary search
solutions.idea: For each offer as the earlier booking, find the first offer starting after it ends and take the best pay from there on.

followups: Allow up to k bookings instead of two. (Hint: DP over offers sorted by end.)
Solve it with a min-heap of offers keyed by end day while scanning by start. What does the heap hold?
